dstask

Single binary terminal-based TODO manager with git-based sync + markdown notes per task




Dstask is a personal task tracker designed to help you focus. It is similar to [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) but uses git to synchronise instead of a special protocol. If you're at home in the terminal, and with solving the occasional merge conflict, then dstask is for you! https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589d06fd-7486-46e4-b838-ce85af12f0fc [Video courtesy of xGoivo -- thanks!](https://www.reddit.com/r/taskwarrior/comments/1o7itzg/what_do_you_guys_think_about_this_taskwarrior/) ## Features - Powerful context system (automatically applies filter/tags to queries and new tasks) - **Git powered sync**/undo/resolve ([passwordstore.org](https://www.passwordstore.org/) style) which means no need to set up a sync server, and syncing between devices is easy! - Task listing won't break with long task text - `note` command -- edit a **full markdown note** for each task. **Checklists are useful here.** - `open` command -- **open URLs found in specified task** (including notes) in the browser - zsh/bash completion (including tags and projects in current context) for speed; PowerShell completion on Windows - A single statically-linked binary - import tool which can import GitHub issues or taskwarrior tasks. ## Non-features - Collaboration. This is a personal task tracker. Use another system for projects that involve multiple people. Note that it can still be beneficial to use dstask to track what you are working on in the context of a multi-person project tracked elsewhere. ## Requirements - Git - A 256-color capable terminal ## Installation 1. Copy the executable (from the [releases page][releases]) to somewhere in your PATH. - Linux/macOS: name it `dstask` and mark it executable (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/`). - Windows: use `dstask.exe` and place it in a directory on `PATH` (e.g. `%USERPROFILE%\bin`). 1. Enable shell completions: - Bash: add `source <(dstask bash-completion)` to your `.bashrc`. - Zsh: add `dstask zsh-completion > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_dstask` or source completions in your `~/.zshrc`. - PowerShell (Windows): see section "PowerShell completion" below. 1. Set up an alias in your `.bashrc`: `alias task=dstask` or `alias t=dstask` to make task management slightly faster. 1. Create or clone a `~/.dstask` git repository for the data, if you haven't already: - Linux/macOS: `mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init` - Windows: `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.dstask && git -C %USERPROFILE%\.dstask init` ## PowerShell completion Save the completion script to a file and source it in your PowerShell profile: ```powershell dstask powershell-completion > ~\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\dstask-completion.ps1 Add-Content $PROFILE '. ~/Documents/WindowsPowerShell/dstask-completion.ps1' ``` ## Usage Run `dstask help` for usage information. ### Basic Commands - `dstask add [tags] [project:name] [priority:P0-P3]` - Add a new task - `dstask` or `dstask next` - Show next tasks to work on - `dstask start` - Start working on a task - `dstask stop` - Stop working on a task - `dstask done` - Mark a task as complete - `dstask edit` - Edit a task - `dstask note` - Edit the markdown note for a task - `dstask open` - Open URLs in task and note - `dstask show-open` - Show all open tasks - `dstask show-resolved` - Show completed tasks - `dstask show-paused` - Show paused tasks - `dstask context ` - Switch to a context (filter) - `dstask sync` - Synchronise with git remote ### Task Properties - **Priority**: P0 (highest), P1, P2 (default), P3 (lowest) - **Tags**: Add with `+tag`, remove with `-tag` - **Projects**: Set with `project:name` - **Due dates**: Set with `due:YYYY-MM-DD` - **Status**: open, active, paused, resolved ### Contexts Contexts automatically filter tasks and apply tags to new tasks: ```bash dstask context work dstask add finish report # automatically tagged with +work dstask # shows only work tasks dstask context -- # clear context ``` ### Git Sync Sync your tasks across devices using git: ```bash # Set up sync on first device cd ~/.dstask git remote add origin git push -u origin ma 9937 characters elided riority:P1 dstask add from-template ``` ## Best Practices - Create contexts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus. - Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most. - Keep task summaries brief. Use the note field for details, checklists, and context. - Use dstask to track things you might forget, rather than everything. SNR is important. Don't track tasks for the sake of it, and don't track _ideas_. Track ideas separately. - Spend regular time reviewing tasks. You'll probably find some you've already resolved, and many you've forgotten. The `show-unorganised` command is good for this. - Try to work through tasks from the top of the list. Dstask sorts by priority then creation date -- the most important tasks are at the top. - Use `start`/`stop` to mark what you're genuinely working on right now; it makes resuming work faster. Paused tasks will be slightly highlighted, so you won't lose track of them. `show-paused` helps if they start to pile up. - Keep a [github-style check list](https://help.github.com/en/articles/about-task-lists) in the markdown note of complex or procedural tasks - Failing to get started working? Start with the smallest task - Record only required tasks. Track ideas separately, else your task list will grow unboundedly! - set `DSTASK_CONTEXT` in a `.envrc` per-project repository. With direnv, this allows you to automatically switch context ## Database The default database location is: - Linux/macOS: `~/.dstask/` - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dstask` It can be configured by the environment variable `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`. ## Integration of fuzzy finders Instead of passing task IDs to commands, a fuzzy finder like [*fzf*](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) can be used to search tasks by their summary instead. This is not part of dstask itself, but can be achieved by defining a shell wrapper like this in your `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`: ```bash function dstask () { local has_double_dash subcommand if (( $# == 1 || $# == 2 )); then has_double_dash="$( [[ "$1" == "--" || "$2" == "--" ]] && echo "1" || echo "0" )" subcommand="$( [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && echo "$2" || echo "$1" )" if (( $# == 1 || has_double_dash )) && \ [[ "${subcommand}" =~ ^(done|edit|note|open|remove|start|stop)$ ]] then command dstask show-open $( (( has_double_dash )) && echo "--" ) \ | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .summary] | @tsv' \ | fzf --delimiter='\t' --nth=2 --accept-nth=1 --preview='DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1 dstask {1} --' \ | xargs -n1 dstask "${subcommand}" return fi fi command dstask "$@" } ``` The wrapper function checks if dstask was called with a subcommand missing the task ID, and if so uses the `show-open` command to get a list of tasks to choose from. `--` can be used to ignore the current context for the fuzzy search. All other commands are passed directly to dstask. ## Alternatives Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal. - [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell - [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue - [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support - [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli) - [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager - [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy ## FAQ > Does dstask encrypt tasks? Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote repository encrypted, you may consider [git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or [git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the tools themselves. > Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter? Yes. 1. Set a context: 2. Run a modify command without and ID 3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers. You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command. > Is there a GUI or web interface? Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go via a smartphone: . It's in early stages but is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people. > Has dstask been featured in a magazine? Yes! :-) [releases]: https://github.com/naggie/dstask/releases

Contexts automatically filter tasks and apply tags to new tasks:

```bash
dstask context work
dstask add finish report  # automatically tagged with +work
dstask                    # shows only work tasks
dstask context --          # clear context
```

### Git Sync

Sync your tasks across devices using git:

```bash
# Set up sync on first device
cd ~/.dstask
git remote add origin <your-repo-url>
git push -u origin master

# On other devices
git clone <your-repo-url> ~/.dstask

# To sync
dstask sync
```

### Templates

Create task templates for recurring patterns:

```bash
dstask add template +template project:meetings priority:P1
dstask add from-template <template-id>
```

## Best Practices

- Create contexts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus.
- Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most.
- Keep task summaries brief. Use the note field for details, checklists, and context.
- Use dstask to track things you might forget, rather than everything. SNR is important. Don't track tasks for the sake of it, and don't track _ideas_. Track ideas separately.
- Spend regular time reviewing tasks. You'll probably find some you've already resolved, and many you've forgotten. The `show-unorganised` command is good for this.
- Try to work through tasks from the top of the list. Dstask sorts by priority then creation date -- the most important tasks are at the top.
- Use `start`/`stop` to mark what you're genuinely working on right now; it makes resuming work faster. Paused tasks will be slightly highlighted, so you won't lose track of them. `show-paused` helps if they start to pile up.
- Keep a [github-style check list](https://help.github.com/en/articles/about-task-lists) in the markdown note of complex or procedural tasks
- Failing to get started working? Start with the smallest task
- Record only required tasks. Track ideas separately, else your task list will grow unboundedly!
- set `DSTASK_CONTEXT` in a `.envrc` per-project repository. With direnv, this allows you to automatically switch context

## Database

The default database location is:

- Linux/macOS: `~/.dstask/`
- Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dstask`

It can be configured by the environment variable `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`.

## Integration of fuzzy finders

Instead of passing task IDs to commands, a fuzzy finder like [*fzf*](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) can be used to
search tasks by their summary instead. This is not part of dstask itself, but can be achieved by defining a shell
wrapper like this in your `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`:

```bash
function dstask () {
    local has_double_dash subcommand

    if (( $# == 1 || $# == 2 )); then
        has_double_dash="$( [[ "$1" == "--" || "$2" == "--" ]] && echo "1" || echo "0" )"
        subcommand="$( [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && echo "$2" || echo "$1" )"
        if (( $# == 1 || has_double_dash )) && \
            [[ "${subcommand}" =~ ^(done|edit|note|open|remove|start|stop)$ ]]
        then
            command dstask show-open $( (( has_double_dash )) && echo "--" ) \
                | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .summary] | @tsv' \
                | fzf --delimiter='\t' --nth=2 --accept-nth=1 --preview='DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1 dstask {1} --' \
                | xargs -n1 dstask "${subcommand}"
            return
        fi
    fi

    command dstask "$@"
}
```

The wrapper function checks if dstask was called with a subcommand missing the task ID, and if so uses the `show-open`
command to get a list of tasks to choose from. `--` can be used to ignore the current context for the fuzzy search. All
other commands are passed directly to dstask.

## Alternatives

Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal.

- [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell
- [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue
- [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support
- [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli)
- [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager
- [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy

## FAQ

> Does dstask encrypt tasks?

Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote
repository encrypted, you may consider
[git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or
[git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been
tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the
tools themselves.

> Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter?

Yes.

1. Set a context:
2. Run a modify command without and ID
3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context

This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before
modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of
potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers.

You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command.

> Is there a GUI or web interface?

Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto
has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go
via a smartphone: <https://github.com/botto/dstask-gui> . It's in early stages but
is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people.

> Has dstask been featured in a magazine?

Yes! <https://www.linux-magazine.com/Issues/2021/246/dstask> :-)

# dstask-import

usage: `dstask-import github|tw`

dstask-import is a tool to synchronize between external services or tools, and dstask.
At this point it supports importing from:

* taskwarrior
* GitHub

See below for details on each

## Taskwarrior

The import functionality is designed to aid with the transition from using taskwarrior to dstask.

Before installing dstask, you may want to export your taskwarrior database:

    task export > taskwarrior.json

After un-installing taskwarrior and installing dstask, to import the tasks to
dstask after initialising the dstask database with git:

    mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init
    dstask-import tw < taskwarrior.json

Note that the import process is lossy due to subtle differences between taskwarrior and dstask.

## GitHub

You can import issues from GitHub repositories into dstask.

### Authentication

To import from private repositories, you'll need a GitHub personal access token.
For public repositories, authentication is optional but recommended to avoid rate limits.

### Usage

To import issues from a GitHub repository:

    dstask-import github <owner>/<repo>

You can also import from multiple repositories by running the command multiple times.

# Moving from Taskwarrior

## Importing data

Please see the [dstask-import tw instructions](dstask-import.md#taskwarrior) to import taskwarrior tasks.

## Using dstask

Commands and syntax are deliberately very similar to taskwarrior. Here are the exceptions:

  * The command is (nearly) always the first argument. Eg, `task eat some add bananas` won't work, but `task add eat some bananas` will. If there's an ID, it can proceed the command but doesn't have to.
  * Priorities are added by the keywords `P0` `P1` `P2` `P3`. Lower number is more urgent. Default is `P2`. For example `task add eat some bananas P1`. The keyword can be anywhere after the command.
  * Action is always the first argument. Eg, `task eat some add bananas` won't work, but `task add eat some bananas` will.
  * Contexts are defined on-the-fly, and are added to all new tasks if set. Use `--` to ignore current context in any command.

Usage: dstask undo <n>

Undo the last <n> commits on the repository. Default is 1. Use

to revert/rebase/merge on the dstask repository itself. The dstask repository
is at ~/.dstask by default.

'Usage: dstask add [template:<id>] [task summary] [--]
Example: dstask add Fix main web page 500 error +bug P1 project:website

Add a task, returning the git commit output which contains the task ID, used
later to reference the task.

Tags, project and priority can be added anywhere within the task summary.

Add -- to ignore the current context. / can be used when adding tasks to note
any words after.

"Usage: dstask [bash|zsh|fish]-completion

    source <(dstask bash-completion)
    source <(dstask zsh-completion)

"
---help_context.txt---
'Usage: dstask context <filter>
Example: dstask context +work -bug
Example: dstask context none

Set a global filter consisting of a project, tags or antitags. Subsequent new
tasks and most commands will then have this filter applied automatically.

For example, if you were to run "task add fix the webserver," the given task
would then have the tag "work" applied automatically.

To reset to no context, run: dstask context none

Context can also be set with the environment variable DSTASK_CONTEXT. If set, 
this context string will override the context stored on disk.
'

'Usage dstask template <id> [task summary] [--]
Example: dstask template Fix main web page 500 error +bug P1 project:website
Example: dstask template 34 project:

If valid task ID is supplied, a copy of the task is created as a template. If
no ID is given, a new task template is created.

Tags, project and priority can be added anywhere within the task summary.

Add -- to ignore the current context. / can be used when adding tasks to note
any words after

Template tasks are not displayed with "show-open" or "show-next" commands.
Their intent is to act as a readily available task template for commonly used
or repeated tasks.

To create a new task from a template use the command:
"dstask add template:<id> [task summary] [--]"

import subprocess, os, shutil, json
REPO="/tmp/dstfresh"
def runq(args, input_data=None, extra_env=None, repo=REPO):
    env=dict(os.environ); env["DSTASK_GIT_REPO"]=repo
    if extra_env: env.update(extra_env)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, input=input_data, env=env)
    return p
def show(cmd=["show-open"], repo=REPO):
    p=runq(cmd, repo=repo)
    try: return json.loads(p.stdout)
    except: return p.stdout
def fresh(repo=REPO): shutil.rmtree(repo, ignore_errors=True)
PY

import pty, os, subprocess, struct, fcntl, termios, select
def run_pty(args, cols=80, rows=24, env_extra=None, repo="/tmp/dstfresh", inp=None):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0,0))
    env=dict(os.environ); env["DSTASK_GIT_REPO"]=repo; env["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=slave, env=env, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    out=b""
    if inp:
        os.write(master, inp)
    while True:
        try:
            r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],2)
            if not r: break
            d=os.read(master, 65536)
            if not d: break
            out+=d
        except OSError: break
    try: p.wait(timeout=2)
    except: p.kill()
    print(f"args={args} env={env_extra} exit={p.returncode} out={out!r}")
    return p, out
PY

 for f in "$@"; do echo "---FILE $f---" >> /tmp/editorlog.txt; cat "$f" >> /tmp/editorlog.txt 2>&1; echo "---END---" >> /tmp/editorlog.txt; ls -l "$f" >> /tmp/editorlog.txt; done
 echo "stdout from editor"
 echo "stderr from editor" >&2
 # if DSTASK_TEST_EDITOR_MODE set via env file? just append marker if file writable
 for f in "$@"; do printf "\nEDITED-IN-EDITOR\n" >> "$f"; done
 exit 0
EOS

exec(open("/tmp/compact.py").read()); exec(open("/tmp/summ.py").read())

PY"}

def interact(args, inputs, repo="/tmp/dstfresh", env_extra=None, cols=80, rows=24):

import pty, os, subprocess, struct, fcntl, termios, select
def run_ptyq(args, cols=80, rows=24, env_extra=None, repo="/tmp/dstfresh"):
    master, slave = pty.openpty(); fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0,0))
    env=dict(os.environ); env["DSTASK_GIT_REPO"]=repo; env["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=slave, env=env, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave); out=b""
    while True:
        try:
            r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],2)
            if not r: break
            d=os.read(master,65536)
            if not d: break
            out+=d
        except OSError: break
    p.wait(); return p.returncode,out.decode(errors='replace')

    text=re.sub(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}(?:\.\d+)? \+0000 UTC","<TS>",text)
    text=re.sub(r"^\d{4}/\d{2}/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} ","<LOGTS> ",text,flags=re.M)
    text=re.sub(r"^ Date: .*"," Date: <DATE>",text,flags=re.M)
    text=re.sub(r"dstask\.\d+\.","dstask.<RAND>.",text)
    text=re.sub(r"\[master [0-9a-f]+\]","<GITCOMMIT>",text)
    return text
def run_sequence(ops, binary, repo):
    shutil.rmtree(repo,ignore_errors=True)
    uuidmap={}
    transcript=[]
    for op in ops:
        if isinstance(op, dict):
            args=op.get("args",[]); inp=op.get("input"); envx=op.get("env",{})
            if "setup" in op:
                op["setup"](repo); transcript.append(f"SETUP {op.get('label','')}\n"); continue
        else:
            args=op; inp=None; envx={}
        env=dict(os.environ); env["DSTASK_GIT_REPO"]=repo
        for k,v in envx.items(): env[k]=v.replace("<REPO>",repo) if isinstance(v,str) else v
        p=subprocess.run([binary]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,input=inp,env=env)
        transcript.append(f">>> {args} inp={inp!r} env={envx} RC={p.returncode}\nOUT:{normalize(p.stdout,repo,uuidmap)!r}\nERR:{normalize(p.stderr,repo,uuidmap)!r}\n")
    # filesystem state (excluding .git internals except dstask state size names)
    files=[]
    for root,dirs,fs in os.walk(repo):
        if ".git" in dirs and root==repo:
            # include .git/dstask names only
            pass
        dirs.sort(); fs.sort()
        for f in fs:
            path=os.path.join(root,f); rel=os.path.relpath(path,repo)
            if rel.startswith(".git/") and not rel.startswith(".git/dstask/"): continue
            try: content=open(path,errors='replace').read()
            except: content="<binary>"
            files.append(f"FILE {normalize(rel,repo,uuidmap)}:\n{normalize(content,repo,uuidmap)}")
    transcript.append("\n".join(files))
    gl=subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"log","--format=%s%n%b==="],capture_output=True,text=True)
    transcript.append("GITLOG:\n"+normalize(gl.stdout,repo,uuidmap)+normalize(gl.stderr,repo,uuidmap))
    st=subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"status","--short"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    transcript.append("GITSTATUS:\n"+normalize(st.stdout,repo,uuidmap))
    return "\n".join(transcript)
def compare(name,ops):
    a=run_sequence(ops,ORIG,"/tmp/cmp_orig")
    b=run_sequence(ops,MINE,"/tmp/cmp_mine")

        print(f"PASS {name}"); return True
    print(f"FAIL {name}")
    diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(a.splitlines(),b.splitlines(),"orig","mine",lineterm=""))
    for line in diff[:300]: print(line)
    if len(diff)>300: print(f"... {len(diff)-300} more diff lines")
    return False

func padRight(s string, width int) string {
	s = truncRunes(s, width)
	for runeLen(s) < width {
		s += " "
	}
	return s
}

func computeWidths(headers []string, rows [][]string, termWidth int) []int {
	widths := make([]int, len(headers))
	for i, h := range headers {
		widths[i] = runeLen(h)
	}
	for _, row := range rows {
		for i, cell := range row {
			if i < len(widths) && runeLen(cell) > widths[i] {
				widths[i] = runeLen(cell)
			}
		}
	}
	total := 0
	for _, w := range widths {
		total += w
	}
	if len(widths) > 1 {
		total += 2 * (len(widths) - 1)
	}
	for total > termWidth {
		maxIdx := 0
		for i, w := range widths {
			if w > widths[maxIdx] {
				maxIdx = i
			}
		}
		if widths[maxIdx] <= 0 {
			break
		}
		widths[maxIdx]--
		total--
	}
	return widths
}

func renderPlainTable(headers []string, rows [][]string, styles []string) {
	termWidth, _ := terminalSize()
	widths := computeWidths(headers, rows, termWidth)
	// Header.
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("\x1b[4;38;5;250;48;5;232m")
	for i, h := range headers {
		if i > 0 {
			b.WriteString("  ")
		}
		b.WriteString(padRight(h, widths[i]))
	}

364:func extractURLs(s string) []string {
	// IPv6 literal.
	if strings.HasPrefix(host, "[") {
		return true
	}
	// Strip port.
	if idx := strings.LastIndex(host, ":"); idx >= 0 {
		host = host[:idx]
	}
	if host == "localhost" {
		return true
	}
	// IPv4 validation.
	parts := strings.Split(host, ".")
	isNumeric := true
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part == "" {
			isNumeric = false
			break
		}
		for _, c := range part {
			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
				isNumeric = false
			}
		}
	}
	if isNumeric {
		if len(parts) != 4 {
			return false
		}
		for _, part := range parts {
			n, err := strconv.Atoi(part)
			if err != nil || n > 255 {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	if len(parts) < 2 {
		return false
	}
	tld := strings.ToLower(parts[len(parts)-1])
	return validTLDs[tld]
}

func extractURLs(s string) []string {
	matches := urlRegexp.FindAllString(s, -1)
	var out []string
	for _, m := range matches {
		m = trimURLPunctuation(m)
		if m != "" && isValidURLCandidate(m) {
			out = append(out, m)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func CommandOpen(ts *TaskSet, state State, q Query) {
	q.MustHaveIDs()
	q.MustNoOperators()
	for _, id := range q.IDs {
		task := ts.GetTaskByID(id)
		urls := append(extractURLs(task.Summary), extractURLs(task.Notes)...)
		if len(urls) == 0 {
			MustFail("no URLs found in task %d", id)
		}
		for _, u := range urls {
			cmd := exec.Command("xdg-open", u)
			if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
				MustFail("Failed to open browser")
			}
		}
	}
}

func CommandContext(state State, q Query) {
	if len(os.Args) <= 2 {
		fmt.Println(state.Context.String())
		if !state.contextFromEnv {
			SaveState(state)
		}
		return
	}
	if state.contextFromEnv {
		MustFail("setting context not allowed while DSTASK_CONTEXT is set")
	}
	if len(os.Args) > 2 && os.Args[2] == "none" {
		state.Context = Query{}
		SaveState(state)
		return
	}
	if len(q.IDs) > 0 {
		MustFail("context cannot contain IDs")
	}
	if q.Text != "" {
		MustFail("context cannot contain text")
	}
	state.Context = q
	SaveState(state)
}

func CommandUndo() {
	n := 1
	if len(os.Args) > 2 {
		parsed, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Args[2])
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, helpUndo)
			return
		}
		n = parsed
	}
	runGitCmd("revert", "--no-edit", fmt.Sprintf("HEAD~%d..", n))
